newsitem.title: FINLAND: POLAR SEES SLIGHT OP LOSS IN EARLY 1997.
newsitem.headline: POLAR SEES SLIGHT OP LOSS IN EARLY 1997.

text.p: Finnish construction group Polar said on Wednesday its building operations would incur a slight operating loss in the early part of the year, and that its full-year 1997 operating result would not improve on 1996.

"The early-year operating result of (the group's) building operations will be a slight loss. For this reason, the whole group's 1997 operating result is not expected to improve on the previous year," Polar said in a statement.

"The 1997 earnings prospects of the group's building operations have weakened during the early part of the year mainly due to weakening of the profit expectations of the Helsinki region office building unit and of the eastern Finland unit," Polar said.

Polar's CEO Arto Ihto said by telephone the statement was issued because the group's previous forecast was that operating profits would improve in 1997, but that its view on overall market strength had not changed.
"What we have said before on the market strength is still valid," he said.
"This is a solely Polar-centered statement," he added.
Ihto said said in Polar's 1996 annual report the group's prospects for 1997 were better than last year, both for construction and the real estate business.
On construction it said: "The cyclic upswing that started at the end of last year is expected to last."

In 1996, Polar made a 54 million markka operating profit, with 28 million markka from construction and 65 million markka from real estate. It booked 39 million markka in operating charges from group administration and goodwill in 1996.
